items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-01-13
items.q: I've asked Mr. Russell. I've asked Mr. Crawford. I've asked this boy Meads in Omaha, Nebraska. And asked him to try to find those two funeral marches for me, but they can't be found.

ctx.x: My name is Joseph Clark. I was born February 12, 1894. My father's name is Aaron Warren Clark. He was born in 1876. He died September 14, 1894. He was a musician before I was born. And after I was born, before I was born, he'd taken sick. And he told my mother never to let me play a wind instrument. And my mother always kept that pruned into me never to play a wind instrument. And after I began to grow, it just looked like I'd taken a feeling from music. And I was a very small boy. I used to follow bands. And she…
I wanted to ask you a couple questions. Where was your father born, you said?

items.title: Joseph "Red" Clark Interview, 1959-11-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Marjorie Zander. >> [INTERVIEWEE] Bill Russell. ... [INTERVIEWER] I wanted to ask about a studio. Where was that 6th Street? >> [INTERVIEWEE] That's, uh, Mr. Russell I really don't know, I really don't know the number of that house.

ctx.x: And I'm Dick Allen. And let's see, we're recording this at 1717 Drive in the back in Clark's kitchen. And today's date is November? The 11th. November the 11th, 1959. Okay. Let's see.
